config.title: Berlin's Most Beautiful U-Bahn Stations - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which stations are worth getting off at, how far each one is from Alexanderplatz, and what ticket the trip needs.

items.q: Which is the most beautiful U-Bahn station in Berlin?
items.a: **Two answers, depending on how far you will travel.** If you want one stop and no planning, it is **Museumsinsel** on the U5, three minutes from Alexanderplatz: a deep blue barrel vault with 6,662 points of light, 16 metres below the Spreekanal, based on Schinkel's 1816 stage set for The Magic Flute. If you are willing to ride 28 minutes out on the U3, it is **Heidelberger Platz**, a cross-groin vault on stone piers from 12 October 1913 that reads more like a church than a station.

items.q: Can I see the Ishtar Gate tiles anywhere while the Pergamon Museum is closed?
items.a: **The gate itself, no. Tiles from the same project, yes.** The Pergamon Museum has been fully closed since October 2023 and the Ishtar Gate is not expected back on display until the 2030s. The stylised palms at the entrances of **Klosterstraße** station on the U2 were made with the same brick technique as the gate, using tiles left over when it was assembled. It is one stop east of Alexanderplatz and costs nothing beyond the ride.

items.q: How long does it take to reach the Spandau U-Bahn stations from Alexanderplatz?
items.a: **Forty to forty-eight minutes each way, with one change.** Rohrdamm is about 40 minutes, Paulsternstraße 42, Zitadelle 45, Altstadt Spandau 47 and Rathaus Spandau 48, all on the U2 then the U7. That is a genuine half day there and back, so treat the stations as what you look at on the way to **Spandau's old town and citadel** rather than as the trip itself.

items.q: What ticket do I need to visit several U-Bahn stations in one trip?
items.a: **All of them are inside the AB zone, so the question is only which ticket type.** A single AB ticket is **€4.00** and lasts 120 minutes, but only in one direction, and return journeys are not allowed on it. One out and back to a single area therefore needs two singles, €8.00. The moment you are heading to more than one corner of the city, the **24-hour AB ticket at €11.20** is cheaper. Prices checked on 26 August 2026.

items.q: When is the best time of day to look at Berlin U-Bahn stations?
items.a: **Between 10:00 and 15:00 on a weekday.** Outside the rush the platforms are half empty and nobody is trying to get past you. Stand behind the ribbed paving near the platform edge, which is a guidance line for blind passengers rather than a photo mark. BVG does not permit tripods, lights or flash rigs on its stations, and anything commercial needs written permission first.

items.q: Are any of these stations on the BerlinWalk route?
items.a: **Two are directly underneath it.** The free walking tour covers eleven stops and sixteen places over about 3 km in roughly 2 hours, and the route passes over **Rotes Rathaus** station near the start and **Museumsinsel** in the middle. The medieval town hall whose vault gave Rotes Rathaus station its mushroom-cap columns stood a few metres from where the group gathers. Look at either station properly before the walk or after it ends at Hackescher Markt.
